privacy.note: IDX says its ForgetMe PII Removal scans over 100 data-broker websites and requests deletion of unauthorized profiles.

openness.note: IDX Privacy is a closed commercial privacy and identity-protection service.

portability.note: IDX automates removal and confirms progress inside its platform, so ongoing benefit is service-bound.

respect.note: The service reduces exposure on public-info sites, but it also bundles identity, password and monitoring features under one vendor.

accessibility.note: IDX's consumer plan page presents PII removal as an automatic feature alongside identity and privacy protections.

economical.note: IDX Privacy is sold as a paid consumer protection plan rather than a free public utility.

products.description: A paid identity and privacy suite whose ForgetMe feature scans broker sites and submits removal requests.

products.name: Onerep

privacy.note: Onerep says it scans hundreds of people-search sites and handles recurring opt-out procedures.

openness.note: Onerep is a closed commercial removal service rather than a public or open-source opt-out directory.

portability.note: It provides removal tracking and family plans, but the automation remains tied to an active subscription.

respect.note: The service focuses on people-search removals rather than broader surveillance reduction, which is useful but narrow.

accessibility.note: Onerep emphasizes automated scanning and repeated removals to avoid manual broker-by-broker opt-outs.

economical.note: Onerep publishes individual and family subscription prices, positioning itself below many reputation-management services but not free.

products.description: A paid people-search removal service with recurring scans and family-plan coverage.

products.name: Norton Privacy Monitor

privacy.note: Norton says Privacy Monitor helps find personal data and provides broker opt-out instructions; automatic removal requires Assistant or related plan support.

openness.note: Norton Privacy Monitor is part of a closed commercial security suite.

portability.note: The useful scans, reminders and assisted removals live inside Norton's account and product bundle.

respect.note: The Assistant can rescan and resubmit removals, but the base monitor can be more of a guided manual workflow than a complete remover.

accessibility.note: Norton integrates privacy monitoring into familiar Norton/LifeLock products and provides guided broker-by-broker actions.

economical.note: Privacy Monitor is tied to Norton plans, and automatic removal may require paid Assistant features.

products.description: A Norton/LifeLock privacy monitor that finds broker exposure and can add assisted removals in paid plan contexts.

products.name: McAfee Personal Data Cleanup

privacy.note: McAfee says Personal Data Cleanup scans broker and people-search sites and can send removal requests in higher McAfee+ plans.

openness.note: The feature is part of McAfee's closed commercial security suite.

portability.note: Removal monitoring and automation are plan features rather than portable user-owned data exports.

respect.note: The scan-and-removal flow can reduce exposure, but full-service removal is bundled into paid McAfee products.

accessibility.note: McAfee provides a consumer dashboard for scanning personal info and guiding or automating cleanup.

economical.note: McAfee says guidance is available, but full-service cleanup comes with McAfee+ Advanced and Ultimate plans.

products.description: A McAfee privacy-cleanup feature that scans for broker exposure, with automated removals tied to higher paid plans.

products.name: Experian Privacy Scan

privacy.note: Experian describes privacy scans as tools that search digital records and people-finder sites to identify exposed personal information.

openness.note: Experian's privacy and monitoring tools are proprietary services from a major credit bureau.

portability.note: The scan helps locate exposure, but any ongoing monitoring or removal support stays inside Experian's product ecosystem.

respect.note: The tool can surface useful risks, but Experian's own privacy policy confirms broad credit-bureau data collection and consumer-rights exceptions.

accessibility.note: Experian promotes free scans and alerts that are easy for mainstream users to try.

economical.note: Experian offers a free dark-web email scan and privacy scan entry point, though paid identity products may be promoted.

products.description: A mainstream privacy and dark-web scan from Experian, useful for exposure discovery but tied to a credit-bureau ecosystem.

products.name: Credit Karma Identity Monitoring

privacy.note: Credit Karma says its free identity monitoring alerts users if personal information is exposed in public data breaches.

openness.note: Credit Karma is a proprietary Intuit service, not an open-source monitor.

portability.note: Intuit says users can download, update and delete their data through Intuit Account, but monitoring itself remains account-bound.

respect.note: The service is free and useful, but it is connected to a financial-product ecosystem that uses shared data to personalize offers.

accessibility.note: Credit Karma offers no-cost identity and credit monitoring through a mainstream consumer account.

economical.note: Credit Karma describes identity monitoring and credit monitoring as free services.

products.description: A free breach and identity-monitoring feature inside Credit Karma, useful but tied to a data-rich financial platform.

products.name: JustDeleteMe

privacy.note: JustDeleteMe is a directory of direct links to delete accounts from web services.

openness.note: The project links to GitHub and accepts contributions for the account-deletion directory.

portability.note: It helps users leave individual services directly rather than locking cleanup into a subscription.

respect.note: JustDeleteMe exposes the difficulty of deleting accounts and sends users to the service's deletion path.

accessibility.note: The directory uses search and difficulty ratings to make account deletion paths easier to find.

economical.note: The directory is free to use online.

products.description: A free, open directory of direct account-deletion links and difficulty ratings for common web services.

products.name: Simple Opt Out

privacy.note: Simple Opt Out collects deep links to opt out of data sharing by more than 100 companies.

openness.note: The site is a public opt-out directory, though not a full open-source automated removal service.

portability.note: It points users to each company's own opt-out path, so users keep direct control over the request.

respect.note: The site is explicitly designed to make company data-sharing opt-outs easier to find.

accessibility.note: The page is a simple list of companies, links and opt-out tips rather than a complex dashboard.

economical.note: Simple Opt Out is free to use.

products.description: A free directory of direct links and tips for opting out of data sharing by common companies.

products.name: California DROP

privacy.note: California's Delete Request and Opt-out Platform lets eligible consumers request deletion of personal information from registered data brokers.

openness.note: DROP is a public state platform created under California's Delete Act rather than a private subscription service.

portability.note: The platform provides requests to registered brokers, but it is limited by legal eligibility and broker compliance rather than universal deletion power.

respect.note: The state describes DROP as free and easy to access, with brokers required to continue deleting consumer data every 45 days after processing begins.

accessibility.note: DROP centralizes broker deletion requests rather than requiring consumers to contact each registered broker manually.

economical.note: The platform is free for consumers to use.

products.description: California's public data-broker deletion request platform, useful for eligible residents and a model for rights-based privacy cleanup.

products.name: Google Security Checkup

privacy.note: Google Security Checkup gives personalized recommendations to review security events, devices and extra protections for a Google Account.

openness.note: The checkup is a closed Google Account tool rather than an open-source or independently portable security audit.

portability.note: It helps secure Google Account settings, but its recommendations and state are specific to Google's ecosystem.

respect.note: The tool is useful for reducing account takeover risk, while still requiring users to manage security inside Google's account system.

accessibility.note: Google presents Security Checkup as a step-by-step tool with personalized, actionable recommendations.

economical.note: Security Checkup is available without a separate paid subscription.

products.description: Google's free account-security review for devices, events, recovery options and recommended protections.

products.name: Google Password Checkup

privacy.note: Google Password Manager's Password Checkup checks saved passwords for compromise, weakness and reuse.

openness.note: The checkup is a proprietary Google password-manager feature rather than an open-source breach-checking utility.

portability.note: It can help fix risky accounts, but it is most useful when passwords are stored in Google's password manager.

respect.note: The tool warns about compromised passwords and helps users change them, though it reinforces Google-account-centered password management.

accessibility.note: Google describes Password Checkup as giving personalized advice when compromised or weak passwords are found.

economical.note: Password Checkup is available without a separate paid subscription.

products.description: A free Google Password Manager check for compromised, weak and reused saved passwords.

products.name: Apple Safety Check

privacy.note: Apple Safety Check helps iPhone users quickly review and manage information shared with people and apps.

openness.note: Safety Check is an Apple platform feature, not an open-source or cross-platform safety utility.

portability.note: It is powerful for iPhone/iCloud sharing review but only works in Apple's device ecosystem.

respect.note: The feature is explicitly designed for personal safety, including quickly managing access by people, apps and devices.

accessibility.note: Apple documents Safety Check inside a Personal Safety User Guide with step-by-step support topics.

economical.note: Safety Check is included on supported iPhones with iOS 16 or later rather than sold as a separate subscription.

products.description: Apple's iPhone safety feature for reviewing and revoking sharing, app access and connected-device access.

products.name: Microsoft Account Security

privacy.note: Microsoft account security tools let users manage verification methods, sign-in information and account protection settings.

openness.note: The security dashboard is a proprietary Microsoft Account service rather than an open audit tool.

portability.note: The controls are useful for Microsoft accounts and devices, but security status and settings are ecosystem-bound.

respect.note: Microsoft offers account-protection controls and a privacy dashboard, but users still manage them inside a data-rich Microsoft account.

accessibility.note: Microsoft documents step-by-step ways to add, remove and manage sign-in verification methods.

economical.note: Basic Microsoft account security controls are available to account holders without a separate subscription.

products.description: Microsoft's account dashboard and security-info tools for reviewing sign-in methods, devices and privacy controls.

products.name: Facebook Privacy Checkup

privacy.note: Meta says Privacy Checkup helps users review who can see what they share, account security, how people find them and data settings.

openness.note: Privacy Checkup is a proprietary Facebook feature, not an open or independently auditable privacy tool.

portability.note: The checkup affects Facebook settings rather than providing cross-platform privacy portability.

respect.note: It can reduce oversharing on Facebook, but it does not eliminate Meta's underlying data-driven platform model.

accessibility.note: Meta designed Privacy Checkup as a guided flow through important settings and tips.

economical.note: Facebook Privacy Checkup is available to Facebook users without a separate paid subscription.

products.description: Facebook's guided privacy-settings review for sharing, discoverability, account security and data settings.

products.name: Facebook Security Checkup

privacy.note: Meta's safety guidance points users to Security Checkup to review and add security protections to a Facebook account.

openness.note: Security Checkup is a closed Facebook account feature rather than an open account-security scanner.

portability.note: The checkup is specific to Facebook and Meta account settings rather than reusable across services.

respect.note: It helps users enable protections like login alerts and two-factor authentication, but stays within Meta's surveillance-advertising ecosystem.

accessibility.note: Facebook Help Center pages describe account-security features such as login alerts and two-factor authentication.

economical.note: Facebook security settings are available without a separate paid subscription.

products.description: Facebook's account-security review path for login alerts, two-factor authentication and account-hardening basics.

products.name: 2FA Directory

privacy.note: 2FA Directory lists services that support two-factor authentication, helping users harden accounts across many sites.

openness.note: The project describes itself on GitHub as an open-source, community-driven directory of services that support 2FA.

portability.note: The directory helps users choose and enable stronger authentication across independent services, not inside one vendor account.

respect.note: It is a neutral reference directory focused on improving account security rather than collecting sensitive account credentials.

accessibility.note: The public site presents categories, service names and supported 2FA methods in a browsable directory.

economical.note: The directory is free to browse.

products.description: An open, community-maintained directory showing which services support two-factor authentication and which methods they offer.

products.name: ReportFraud.gov

privacy.note: ReportFraud.gov lets consumers report fraud, scams and bad business practices to the FTC.

openness.note: The FTC states the site is a government reporting platform, though report handling is not open-source or public by default.

portability.note: Reports are shared with law enforcers for investigation rather than exported as a user-owned case-management workspace.

respect.note: The FTC says reports help investigators see scam patterns and bring cases, while not resolving individual reports directly.

accessibility.note: The FTC redesigned reporting to provide a streamlined consumer experience and advice after filing.

economical.note: Reporting fraud to the FTC is free.

products.description: The FTC's free reporting portal for scams, fraud and bad business practices, with reports shared to law enforcement partners.

products.name: IdentityTheft.gov

privacy.note: IdentityTheft.gov helps people report identity theft and generate an FTC Identity Theft Report and personal recovery plan.

openness.note: The FTC describes IdentityTheft.gov as the federal government's one-stop resource for reporting and recovering from identity theft.

portability.note: The service produces an Identity Theft Report and recovery steps that can be used with businesses and agencies.

respect.note: It gives victims step-by-step recovery guidance, sample letters and reporting support without commercial upsell.

accessibility.note: The site guides users through identity-theft recovery steps and offers resources in a structured assistant flow.

economical.note: The FTC recovery plan and identity-theft report process is free.

products.description: The FTC's free identity-theft reporting and recovery-plan service for creating reports, letters and next steps.

products.name: Internet Crime Complaint Center

privacy.note: IC3 is the FBI's intake form for internet crime, cyber-enabled fraud and cybercrime reports.

openness.note: IC3 is an official public reporting portal, but submitted complaint handling and investigative workflows are not open.

portability.note: IC3 gathers reports for investigative and intelligence purposes rather than acting as a personal case-management tool.

respect.note: The FBI says cybercrime victims should report to IC3 as soon as possible and that rapid reporting can support recovery of lost funds.

accessibility.note: IC3 accepts a wide range of internet-crime complaints and tells users to report even if unsure whether the complaint qualifies.

economical.note: Filing an IC3 complaint is free.

products.description: The FBI's free reporting portal for cyber-enabled fraud, scams and other internet-crime complaints.

products.name: Take It Down
products.brand: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children

privacy.note: Take It Down helps remove or stop the spread of nude, partially nude or sexually explicit images and videos of minors using hashes.

openness.note: NCMEC publicly documents the service, though platform matching and removal depend on participating services.

portability.note: The hash can help participating platforms detect and remove matching content, but it is not a universal internet removal guarantee.

respect.note: NCMEC says the tool creates a digital fingerprint on-device so the image or video does not need to leave the device.

accessibility.note: The service offers resources and support for minors and others helping them respond to explicit content online.

economical.note: NCMEC describes Take It Down as a free service.

products.description: NCMEC's free hash-based tool for minors and trusted adults trying to remove or prevent spread of explicit images.

products.name: StopNCII.org

privacy.note: StopNCII.org is a free tool for adults affected by non-consensual intimate image abuse, using hashes generated from their device.

openness.note: The service publicly explains the case-creation process and limitations, while platform matching depends on participating partners.

portability.note: StopNCII can help on participating platforms, but its FAQ notes it does not prevent sharing across the whole internet.

respect.note: The tool uses on-device hashing so the intimate image itself is not uploaded to StopNCII when creating a case.

accessibility.note: StopNCII provides a step-by-step case flow and explains eligibility and what the tool can and cannot remove.

economical.note: StopNCII describes itself as a free tool.

products.description: A free hash-based tool for adults trying to prevent or limit non-consensual intimate image sharing on participating platforms.
